strongest_bounded_proposition: Specialist synthesis supports slavery and dependency in medieval Tamil South India, including likely extensive enslaved agricultural labour from the thirteenth century onward; this is temporally and regionally relevant to the Pandya-period target.
strongest_unsupported_proposition: Do not infer a uniform slavery regime or prevalence across the entire Pandya polity from Tamil inscriptional evidence.
territorial_practice_summary: Slavery/dependency and enslaved agricultural labour are supported in the Tamil-region context around the 13th century.
legal_state_summary: The evidence is primarily inscriptional/social rather than a single polity-wide legal code.
terminology_category_qualification: Slavery operated inside a wider dependency/caste/temple/agrarian hierarchy; categories were heterogeneous.
temporal_scope_precision: The Cambridge synthesis directly covers South India 500–1500 and identifies thirteenth-century onward agricultural slavery.
evidence_locus: Tamil South India under the broad Pandya-period context
inference_extent: Regional bounded claim; no empire-wide prevalence estimate.
language_access_limitations: English-accessible research packet only; non-English and non-digitized scholarship was not exhaustively searched.

sources.title: Slavery and Dependency in Medieval South India
